output.summary: Approved the G1001 design: a request key (explicit request_key, or sha256 of title, spec and depends_on) stored as a Request-Key trailer on the goal's immutable root commit. new scans goal roots before allocating and after any failed push, recovers an identical request, and refuses a key reused with different contents. Decision made by Claude (root agent) under the owner's standing delegation for Release 1; the four reviewer notes go to implement.

responses.review_design:2:1: disputed: at 54d7e83, plugins/zzzops/zzzops/engine/cli.py:97-100 `session(args, environment=True, preview=False)` raises Refused('usage', '--policy-ref is a read-only preview ...') whenever --policy-ref is set and preview is False, before constructing a Session. cmd_new calls `s = session(a)` at cli.py:328 (no preview=True), before `s.open()` (329) and before any scan, so `new --policy-ref dev --file F` exits 1 with usage on a retry too; session.py:186-187 is a second, unreachable guard for new. The design now states this ordering explicitly in section 4 (keep session(a) ahead of the scan; do not rely on require_writable for it) and lists the test as test 10.

output.summary: Design unchanged in substance. Disputed review_design:2:1: at 54d7e83 cli.py session() (lines 97-100) refuses --policy-ref with usage for every non-preview verb before a Session exists, and cmd_new calls session(a) at line 328 before s.open() and the key scan, so a --policy-ref retry is refused before any scan. Added an explicit ordering note in section 4, test 10 pinning test_policy_ref_is_refused_even_for_a_retry, a note that tests 3 (shared ZZZOPS_NOW) and 9 still need writing, and a decision-record entry.

findings.text: cmd_new control flow runs the key scan before s.require_writable(), but require_writable is also where --policy-ref is refused (session.py:186-187). As written, `new --policy-ref dev --file F` for an existing request returns recovered:true (exit 0), so the already-written test_policy_ref_is_refused_even_for_a_retry (expects usage, exit 1) fails, and a read-only preview flag gets through a write verb. Fix: refuse --policy-ref with the same usage error before the scan, and defer only the write-block and engine checks until after it.

output.summary: Core design is sound. Both attempt-2 fixes check out against 54d7e83 and real git: the deleted-ref refetch closes the same-clone fetch race, and a create-only lease push of an identical oid exits 0 as up to date, so report_up_to_date is needed and correctly scoped. One small fix: the 'scan before require_writable' ordering also bypasses the --policy-ref usage refusal, which contradicts the written test test_policy_ref_is_refused_even_for_a_retry. Refuse --policy-ref before the scan. Non-blocking: the tests lack design test 9 and the shared-clock variant of the concurrency test, and a compound same-clone race remains (a repeat-while-deleted-grows hardening is optional).

findings.text: Concurrency hole in the scan scope (reproduced, not hypothetical). When several `new` calls run in the same clone, call X's fetch can write refs/zzzops/goal/origin/g1000 after call Y's fetch listed the remote. build_snapshot then puts G1000 in Y's snap.deleted (a local ref the fetch did not list). The design excludes snap.deleted from the scan, so Y allocates G1001 and its push succeeds: a duplicate. A throwaway prototype of the design as written failed the 10-thread identical-new test about 1 run in 4 with ids {1000, 1001}. test_a_goal_whose_local_ref_outran_this_fetch_is_recovered_not_duplicated reproduces it deterministically by patching engine.store.build_snapshot so the first snapshot omits g1000. A fix that passed all tests and 10 of 10 threaded runs: when the scan finds no match and snap.deleted is not empty, refetch once and scan again before allocating an id. The implementer may choose another fix, for example scanning deleted tips and confirming a deleted-only match with a refetch.

Root commits are deterministic: the same document, message, committer and ZZZOPS_NOW give the same oid. Two identical calls in the same second build the same commit. The second create-only push is then 'up to date' and returns ok, so both calls report recovered:false for the same single goal. There is still only one goal, so this does no harm. The race tests use a different clock per call so the assertion of exactly one recovered:false stays meaningful.

spec:
Give each `new` request a stable identity: an optional client `request_key` in the new-goal file, defaulting to a hash of the canonical title+spec+depends_on. Record it in the goal document or as a goal-commit trailer. Before allocating an id, and after any non-ok push, scan the fetched goal tips for that key; if found, return the existing goal with `created.recovered: true` instead of allocating another id. Reject a request whose key matches a goal with different contents. Deliberately distinct goals with the same title stay allowed because the key covers the spec. Acceptance: unit tests for an exact retry, a push that lands but reports failure, concurrent identical `new` calls (one goal), a key reused with different contents (refused) and same-title distinct specs (two goals). Dropped versus the old wording: issue-based discovery, lock release and capture checkpoints (R1, R12).

title: Make `zzzops new` idempotent across retries and uncertain pushes
